history.dynasty: Unknown; legendary origins (pre-15th century claimed by secondary sources - verify)
history.summary: Famous for the unique Chamayavilakku ritual in which thousands of men dress as women (sarees, makeup, lamps) and process to the temple - the largest such gathering in Kerala and a major LGBTQ+ congregation. Legend: cowherds breaking a coconut on a stone saw blood drip; astrologers declared it Vanadurga's swayambhu presence, and the cowboys began dressing as girls to offer pooja. Kerala Tourism notes it is the only Kerala temple with no roof over the sanctum sanctorum (verify). The main Chamayavilakku procession runs through the night on the final two days of a 19-day festival. The CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name 'Kollam'; actual town is Kottankulangara (near Chavara), state Kerala. Timings conflict slightly across sources: 5-11 AM / 5-8:30 PM (in3ator/ishtadevata) vs 5 AM-11 PM morning session (thrillophilia, likely a typo for 11 AM) vs 4:30-11 AM (banbanjara) - verify.

name: Kottankulangara Devi Temple
town_description: Kottankulangara is a village near Chavara in Kollam district, Kerala, close to the NH and the Arabian Sea coast. Part of the Chavara mineral-sand belt region, it is a pilgrim hub best known for its Devi temple and the famous Chamayavilakku festival.

travel.railway: Kollam railway station, ~14.5 km; then bus to Chavara
travel.road: Near Chavara on the NH, ~450 m from Chavara bus stand; buses from Kollam reach the temple

visitor_information.best_time: March for the Chamayavilakku (10th-11th Meenam); October to March otherwise
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-11:00 AM and 5:00 PM-8:30 PM (in3ator; matches ishtadevata ritual schedule) - CONFLICT (verify): sources differ on morning close (11 AM vs 11:30 AM) and evening start (4:30/5 PM)
